title: A reproducible method to generate multi-building, multi-climate HVAC operation datasets with a stochastic exploratory controller
author: Domingo, Alonso, et al.

steps.title: Install required simulation frameworks
steps.instruction: Set up a Linux environment (Ubuntu 25.04 host, Docker base image Ubuntu 22.04) on a Google Cloud e2-standard-4 node (4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, Intel Broadwell, x86_64). Install Python, then install Sinergym v3.9.5, BOPTEST v0.7.1 (apply the fix from issue 769), and BOPTEST‑Gym v0.7.0. Verify that the Gym‑compatible interfaces are available for both simulators.

steps.title: Prepare building and climate configurations
steps.instruction: Create configuration files for the five source buildings (IDs: 5Zone, Warehouse, OfficeMedium, ShopWithVanBattery, OfficeGridStorageSmoothing) with the geometry, number of zones and floor area given in Table 1. Create a configuration for the target building using the BOPTEST “bestest_air” testcase (BestestAir / Case 900) with geometry from Table 2. Define three source climates (Tucson AZ – hot desert; New York NY – humid subtropical; Port Angeles WA – marine west coast) as listed in Table 3, and one target climate (Denver CO – semi‑arid continental) from Table 4.

steps.title: Define default rule‑based schedules
steps.instruction: For each source building, encode the occupied/unoccupied hours and heating‑cooling setpoint pairs from Table 9. For the target building, encode the occupied 08:00–17:45 setpoints [21 °C, 24 °C] and unoccupied 18:00–07:45 setpoints [10 °C, 30 °C] from Table 10. These schedules will be used when the default rule‑based controller (RBC) is selected.

steps.title: Implement stochastic exploratory controller
steps.instruction: Program a supervisory controller that, at every 15‑minute step, outputs two scalar actions (Heating Setpoint (°C) and Cooling Setpoint (°C)). The controller alternates between short‑horizon behaviours: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck drift, Ramp, Oscillation, Jump, and Hold‑with‑Noise. Every K steps, where K is uniformly sampled from 10–100, a new behaviour and its duration are sampled. After each update, clip heating and cooling setpoints to the bounds defined for the current dataset (see Table 12) and enforce heating ≤ cooling by swapping if necessary. No minimum deadband is applied. The controller uses the exact hyper‑parameters listed in Table 11 (e.g., OU mean‑reversion rate θ ∈ [0.05, 0.5], noise scale σ ∈ [0.5, 2.0], Ramp increment δ ∈ [0.2, 1.0], Oscillation frequency f ∈ [0.01, 0.1], etc.).

steps.title: Set random seeds and bounds per dataset
steps.instruction: For each building script, set the cooling and heating bounds and the random seed exactly as in Table 12: run_office.py (cool 22.5‑30.0 °C, heat 15.0‑22.5 °C, seed 42); run_5zone.py (cool 23.25‑30.0 °C, heat 12.0‑23.25 °C, seed 42); run_shop.py (cool 22.5‑35.0 °C, heat 10.0‑22.5 °C, seed 42); run_warehouse.py (cool 22.5‑35.0 °C, heat 15.0‑22.5 °C, seed 42); run_bestest_air.py (cool 295.65‑308.15 K, heat 283.15‑295.65 K, seed 42). Use these seeds for all random draws (behaviour selection, parameter sampling, K‑intervals) to guarantee deterministic regeneration of trajectories.

steps.title: Run simulations for each scenario
steps.instruction: For every combination of building, climate, and control policy, launch a Gym episode: call env.reset() to obtain the initial observation, then iterate with a 15‑minute control step until the episode ends. Simulate a full calendar year (Jan 1 00:00 to Dec 31 23:45) for all source‑building scenarios. For the target building training sets, simulate 10 months (exclude the two test months). For the target test sets, simulate the fixed calendar windows January (heat evaluation) and July (cool evaluation) for one month each, using a mixed policy that alternates between RBC and the stochastic controller according to the predefined schedule. Do not include any warm‑up period; start from the simulator’s default initial conditions.

steps.title: Log observations and actions each step
steps.instruction: At each 15‑minute step, send the current heating and cooling setpoints to the environment (Sinergym thermostat actuators or BOPTEST zone setpoint inputs). Receive the observation tuple and record the following variables with their physical units: Room Air Temperature (°C) – arithmetic mean of zone temperatures for multi‑zone EnergyPlus models; Outdoor Air Temperature (°C); Outdoor Humidity (%); Direct Solar Radiation (W/m²); Wind Speed (m/s); Cooling Setpoint (°C); Heating Setpoint (°C); HVAC Power Consumption (W) – instantaneous average electrical power over the timestep, aggregated at the environment level. Ignore reward, done, and info fields for dataset purposes.

steps.title: Export time series to Parquet format
steps.instruction: After each simulation episode, write the collected multivariate time series to a Parquet file. Include metadata columns identifying building name, climate location, control policy (default, chaotic, or mixed), simulation year, and random seed. Ensure that column names match the schema in Table 6 and that units are preserved exactly as indicated.

steps.title: Create training and test dataset splits
steps.instruction: Aggregate the exported Parquet files into the six splits described in Table 5: • train‑source‑all: 5 source buildings × 3 climates × {default, chaotic} = 30 years total. • train‑source‑default: 5 × 3 × {default} = 15 years. • train‑target‑default: 1 target building × 1 climate × {default} = 10 months. • train‑target‑chaotic: 1 × 1 × {chaotic} = 10 months. • test‑target‑heat‑test: 1 × 1 × {mixed policy} = January (1 month). • test‑target‑cool‑test: 1 × 1 × {mixed policy} = July (1 month). Verify that each split contains the exact variables listed in Table 6 and that no additional resampling or aggregation has been performed.

steps.title: Validate reproducibility and performance
steps.instruction: Re‑run a subset of scenarios using the same seeds and pinned software versions (Sinergym v3.9.5, EnergyPlus version bundled with Sinergym, BOPTEST v0.7.1, BOPTEST‑Gym v0.7.0). Confirm that the regenerated Parquet files are byte‑identical to the originals. Optionally record execution times on the reference compute node (e.g., BOPTEST stochastic 3 h 52 m 54.7 s, BOPTEST default 2 h 36 m 37.0 s; Sinergym 5Zone stochastic 40 s, default 29 s, etc.) to ensure the pipeline runs within expected bounds.
